messages.author: 048c0ab7da154daf
messages.subject: Random occupancy model using colext? (1-epsilon)=gamma?
parts:
It it possible to fit the random occupancy model using colext() (or other function) in unmarked?

This is the model where (1-epsilon)=gamma so that occupancy in season t+1 does not depend on occupancy in the previous season. Some models can be fit using separate occupancy models for each season, but then you can't share information about p across seasons.

Thanks

Carl Schwarz

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Random occupancy model using colext? (1-epsilon)=gamma?
parts:
Yes.  Each year has a separate parameter for psi (or one could fit some function that relates the psi values among years).  It's as if there's a new random set of sites for each year.  (Offhand I don't know if the AIC values could be directly compared between occu models and colext models.  But there might be a constant that could be determined to add to the occu AIC values to make model comparisons.  It would be convenient if that constant were zero.)

However, I would wonder how one could assume such independence AND the same exact detection probability among years without a lot of previous data.  I understand that pooling data gets one more precise estimates (but only if one can assume rather than just willing to assume that there's a common detection probability).

Jim

Yes, that is my current thinking and it seem to work. TO allow time covariates over the entire set of seasons, it is not a simple stacking but we need to split the data into separate sets of sites for each season and put all NA's before and after the season of interest

COnsider a study with 3 seasons and 2 visits/season
The history 101101 is broken into 3 pseudo-histories
     10....
     ..11..
     ....01
 Then to allow a separate psi for each season, you add a site covariate to give
 SiteCov  History
     T1     10....
     T2     ..11..
     T3     ....01
and then fit the model with  psi~SiteCov

messages.author: 048c0ab7da154daf
messages.subject: Re: Random occupancy model using colext? (1-epsilon)=gamma?
parts:
Here is my sample code to fit a random occupancy model using the occu() function.  The test data is a 3 seasons of 2 visits/season as indicated by the visits vector in the code. The code assumes that a row.name is available for the input history -- it fails if there is no row name, so you should add a simple row.name such as the site id or 1:nsites. 

library(unmarked)

history <-read.csv('test-random.csv',  header=TRUE, as.is=TRUE, row.names=1)
head(history)

# We need to split the data into separate sets of sites for each season
# and put all NA's before and after the season of interest
# COnsider a study with 3 seasons and 2 visits/season
# The history 101101 is broken into 3 pseudo-histories
#     10....
#     ..11..
#     ....01
# Then to allow a separate psi for each season, you add a site covariate to give
#   SiteCov  History
#     T1     10....
#     T2     ..11..
#     T3     ....01
# and then fit the model with  psi~SiteCov


visits <- c(2,2,2)  # 3 seasons with 2 visits per season
start.visit <- cumsum(c(0,visits[-length(visits)]))+1 # when does season start
end.visit   <- cumsum(visits)  # when does season end

rev.history <- NULL # revised history that isolates each season with NA in front and after the season's data
for(i in 1:length(visits)){
   season.history <- cbind(matrix(NA,nrow=nrow(history),ncol=max(0,start.visit[i]-1)),
                           history[, start.visit[i]:end.visit[i]],
                           matrix(NA,nrow=nrow(history),ncol=max(0,end.visit[length(end.visit)]-end.visit[i])))
   row.names(season.history) <- paste("SEAS.", formatC(i, digits=2, flag='0'),'.',row.names(season.history),sep="")
   names(season.history) <- names(history)  # fix up the visit names
   rev.history<- rbind(rev.history,season.history)
}

# create a site covariate that reflects the different seasons for the rev.history
rev.history.site.cov <- data.frame(Season=rep(paste("SEAS.", formatC(1:length(visits), digits=2, flag='0'),sep=""), each=nrow(history)))
library(unmarked)

history <-read.csv('test-random.csv',  header=TRUE, as.is=TRUE, row.names=1)
head(history)

# We need to split the data into separate sets of sites for each season
# and put all NA's before and after the season of interest
# COnsider a study with 3 seasons and 2 visits/season
# The history 101101 is broken into 3 pseudo-histories
#     10....
#     ..11..
#     ....01
# Then to allow a separate psi for each season, you add a site covariate to give
#   SiteCov  History
#     T1     10....
#     T2     ..11..
#     T3     ....01
# and then fit the model with  psi~SiteCov


visits <- c(2,2,2)  # 3 seasons with 2 visits per season
start.visit <- cumsum(c(0,visits[-length(visits)]))+1 # when does season start
end.visit   <- cumsum(visits)  # when does season end

rev.history <- NULL # revised history that isolates each season with NA in front and after the season's data
for(i in 1:length(visits)){
   season.history <- cbind(matrix(NA,nrow=nrow(history),ncol=max(0,start.visit[i]-1)),
                           history[, start.visit[i]:end.visit[i]],
                           matrix(NA,nrow=nrow(history),ncol=max(0,end.visit[length(end.visit)]-end.visit[i])))
   row.names(season.history) <- paste("SEAS.", formatC(i, digits=2, flag='0'),'.',row.names(season.history),sep="")
   names(season.history) <- names(history)  # fix up the visit names
   rev.history<- rbind(rev.history,season.history)
}

# create a site covariate that reflects the different seasons for the rev.history
rev.history.site.cov <- data.frame(Season=rep(paste("SEAS.", formatC(1:length(visits), digits=2, flag='0'),sep=""), each=nrow(history)))
rev.history.site.cov$Time <- rep(1:length(visits), each=nrow(history))


Seasons <- matrix( rep(c("T1","T2","T3"),each=2), nrow=nrow(rev.history), ncol=ncol(rev.history), byrow=TRUE)


occ.UMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(
  y = rev.history,
  obsCovs=list(Season=Seasons),
  siteCovs=rev.history.site.cov)  
occ.UMF
summary(occ.UMF)
plot(occ.UMF, panels=1)


# Now to fit a model for random occupancy with a separate psi for each season
mod <- occu( ~1 ~Season, data=occ.UMF)

mod 
    
psi.pred.cov <- data.frame(Season=unique(rev.history.site.cov$Season))
psi.pred     <- predict(mod, type="state", newdata=psi.pred.cov)
cbind(psi.pred.cov, psi.pred)

p.pred.cov <- data.frame(one=1)
p.pred <- predict(mod, type="det", newdata=p.pred.cov)
cbind(p.pred.cov, p.pred)


Seasons <- matrix( rep(c("T1","T2","T3"),each=2), nrow=nrow(rev.history), ncol=ncol(rev.history), byrow=TRUE)


occ.UMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(
  y = rev.history,
  obsCovs=list(Season=Seasons),
  siteCovs=rev.history.site.cov)  
occ.UMF
summary(occ.UMF)
plot(occ.UMF, panels=1)


# Now to fit a model for random occupancy with a separate psi for each season but a common p over all season.
mod <- occu( ~1 ~Season, data=occ.UMF)

mod 
    
psi.pred.cov <- data.frame(Season=unique(rev.history.site.cov$Season))
psi.pred     <- predict(mod, type="state", newdata=psi.pred.cov)
cbind(psi.pred.cov, psi.pred)

p.pred.cov <- data.frame(one=1)
p.pred <- predict(mod, type="det", newdata=p.pred.cov)
cbind(p.pred.cov, p.pred)

# Now to fit a model for random occupancy with a time trend across seasons but a common p across all seasons
mod2 <- occu( ~1 ~Time, data=occ.UMF)

mod2 
    
psi.pred.cov <- data.frame(Time=1:length(visits))
psi.pred     <- predict(mod2, type="state", newdata=psi.pred.cov)
cbind(psi.pred.cov, psi.pred)

p.pred.cov <- data.frame(one=1)
p.pred <- predict(mod2, type="det", newdata=p.pred.cov)
cbind(p.pred.cov, p.pred)


# Now to fit a model for random occupancy with a time trend across seasons and a separate p for each season.
mod3 <- occu( ~Season ~Time, data=occ.UMF)

mod3 
    
psi.pred.cov <- data.frame(Time=1:length(visits))
psi.pred     <- predict(mod3, type="state", newdata=psi.pred.cov)
cbind(psi.pred.cov, psi.pred)

p.pred.cov <- data.frame(Season=c("T1","T2","T3"))
p.pred <- predict(mod3, type="det", newdata=p.pred.cov)
cbind(p.pred.cov, p.pred)
